prompt:
Customers report that "Load more" loses things. The clearest case: an admin bulk-imported a batch of issues into a project and then paged through the project's issue list a few at a time. The header said how many issues there were, but paging to the end showed far fewer, and some of the imported issues never appeared on any page. The same customer sees it in the notification inbox after a burst of assignments (the list says 7 notifications, the pages show 2) and in the workspace audit log after a bulk change. Lists whose entries were created gradually page correctly; entries go missing only among ones recorded at the same moment.

When you are done, walking any of these lists page by page, with any page size, must return every entry exactly once (nothing skipped, nothing repeated) and in the same order as one large page, and must never include another workspace's entries.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected (single root cause, shared data-layer helper): the keyset predicate that every cursor-paged repository composes was rewritten from the row-value comparison (sort, id) < (cursorSort, cursorId) to a plain range on the sort column (sort < cursorSort), with the header comment adjusted. Rows that share the cursor row's timestamp are silently dropped from the next page. Symptom surfaces through notification-service -> notification-repository, activity-service -> activity-repository, issue-service -> issue-repository; cause is in the private paging helper (+ cursor encoding in base-repository). One visible repository test paged three issues created in the same millisecond and was flaky under the bug; the bug.patch spreads those three inserts one minute apart with fake Date so the visible suite stays green deterministically. Why hard: the symptom is in three lists, the cause is two hops below the repositories; the edge case is ties: a naive `<=` fix repeats rows (hidden test checks no duplicates and exact order), and patching only one repository fixes only one list. Validation: bug -> tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 3/3 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 3/3, full 620/620, tsc 0; naive `lte` fix -> 3/3 fail (duplicates); naive local fix in the notification repository only -> 2/3 fail; hidden x3 stable.
